review_output: {"summary":"I found no critical local defect in the registration coverage audit, publisher or reader. Some things hold if the stated dependency contract holds. The forward and reverse scans share one read-only RepeatableRead snapshot, and both check the same source and registration revisions on every page. The publisher writes only after a bidirectional audit where every row matched, then checks the revisions again in a ReadCommitted write with a FOR SHARE version lock. The DB guard also checks the registration revision at insert time. The reader drops covered proofs that don't have current revisions. Because the revision is an append-only COUNT, it can't return to an old value and make a stale proof look current. Tenant scope is applied in every query. The fixture tests the race between audit and write, a revoked source, an empty proof and a repeated proof. Running out of the enumeration budget fails closed: it returns \"unavailable\" or throws. The known gaps in other producers, the scheduler and the Serializable payment gate are excluded. One high-severity dependency question blocks approval: the proof only fences changes to verified sources. It does not fence changes to the projection or capture tables, so changing a registration row after publish could leave a proof that still reads as current. I could not see from the supplied text whether older DB guards already make those tables immutable. Other findings: the 'private producer' rule is not enforced in the database; the bijection depends on unique-row constraints; a few time-budget and performance issues; and test gaps. This is a conditional pass, pending the dependencies listed below.","findings":[{"confidence":0.55,"severity":"High","file":"src/lib/live-metric-registration-coverage.ts","area":"stale revisions / truthful completeness","impact":"After a 'covered' proof is recorded, a LiveMetricRegistration row could be deleted or added, or a Capture visitorId or versionId changed, without changing LiveMetricVersion.sourceRevision or the registration ledger COUNT. That ledger only counts verified-source changes. The reader would still say coverage is complete while reporting facts that no longer match what was audited.","required_test":"Publish a matched proof. Then (a) delete or insert a LiveMetricRegistration row, and (b) update a Capture's visitorId or versionId. Each change must either be rejected by the DB or make readMetricCoverage stop returning 'complete'.","issue":"The proof fences only verified-source changes and the metric sourceRevision. It does not fence changes to the projection tables (LiveMetricRegistration, LiveMetricRegistrationCapture). Nothing in the supplied text shows these tables are immutable or append-only, or that changing them bumps a revision. This is a missing dependency, not a confirmed missing guard.","evidence":"The dependency contract says the ledger revision changes on verified-source INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE. The publisher re-checks only the version's sourceRevision and wp20_metric_registration_revision (lines 19-25), and the reader filter (lines 23-25) checks only those two. The fixture inserts the registration in a separate statement from the source verification (lines 25-26), so the projection tables are written on their own.","recommended_fix":"Show that existing triggers make LiveMetricRegistration and LiveMetricRegistrationCapture immutable after insert, block TRUNCATE on them, and only allow deletes by cascade from the parent. If they don't, either fold projection changes into the registration revision or bump LiveMetricVersion.sourceRevision whenever those tables change."},{"confidence":0.6,"severity":"Medium","file":"prisma/migrations/20261015190000_live_metric_registration_coverage_proof/migration.sql","area":"SQL guard permissions / producer identity","impact":"Any code that holds the app DB role can insert a 'registrations'/'covered' row with the current revisions and any registrationCount, and the reader would treat it as complete. The rule that only the private producer can publish is a code convention; the database does not enforce it.","required_test":"Run as the application DB role and insert a covered registrations row with the current revisions but no audit. Expect it to be rejected, or expect the right to insert to be limited to a dedicated producer role or function.","issue":"The registration guard only checks that the revision is fresh and the row is well-formed. It does not check where the proof came from. Privileges are revoked from anon, authenticated and service_role, but not from the role Prisma connects as, which is presumably the owner. The guard also allows covered registrations rows with a NULL revision; the reader ignores those, so they are inert but still writable.","evidence":"In migration 2, lines 8-13 only check when registrationRevision IS NOT NULL. The revokes cover API roles only (lines 19-25 and migration 1 lines 59-67).","recommended_fix":"Move the publish write into a SECURITY DEFINER function owned by a separate role, and REVOKE INSERT on LiveMetricCoverageAudit from the app role. Also require registrationRevision and registrationCount to be NOT NULL whenever kind='registrations' AND status='covered'."},{"confidence":0.45,"severity":"Medium","file":"src/lib/live-metric-registration-audit.ts","area":"identity / enumeration correctness","impact":"Duplicate capture or registration rows per submission would make the forward join return several rows for one s.id. Pagination with LIMIT and the s.id>cursor filter would then silently skip the duplicates that land after a page boundary. The count-equality check could also pass with a duplicated projection, so a non-bijective cohort would be certified.","required_test":"Try to insert a second LiveMetricRegistration with the same (versionId, submissionId) and a second Capture with the same submissionId. Both must fail on a unique constraint.","issue":"The bijection proof (audit.count == projectionCount, all rows matched) is only sound if there are UNIQUE constraints on Capture(submissionId) and Registration(versionId, submissionId). Neither constraint appears in the supplied text.","evidence":"Forward query lines 27-29 use LEFT JOINs without DISTINCT, and the cursor at line 19 is s.id>last. The publisher's equality check is in coverage.ts lines 14-15.","recommended_fix":"Show the unique constraints exist or add them. You could also add a forward-side assertion that no submissionId repeats across the results."},{"confidence":0.6,"severity":"Low","file":"src/lib/live-metric-registration-source-audit.ts","area":"enumeration budget","impact":"In the worst case, the elapsed-time check passes just under 23 s and the next page then makes 3 statements of up to 5 s each, about 15 s. That exceeds the 30 s Prisma transaction timeout. The audit would then throw instead of returning limit_exceeded. It still fails closed, but callers can't tell this apart from a real error. From the measured 100k rows in about 5 s, the advertised budget of 1M rows and 2000 pages can't actually be reached within 23 s.","required_test":"Add a test that fills the 23 s budget, or use a lower injected budget, and check the result is {status:'unavailable', reason:'limit_exceeded'} rather than an exception.","issue":"The time budget is only checked between pages, and each page runs three statements (settings, context with COUNT, rows), each with its own timeout.","evidence":"Lines 17 and 26 (5 s statement_timeout, 23 s check) and line 51 (30 s timeout). Each page calls readAuditContext, which makes 2 queries before the page query.","recommended_fix":"Check the time budget before the reverse scan and before every statement, or lower the per-page limit to about 30 s minus 3×statement_timeout. Read the context once per transaction instead of once per page. Document the budget that can actually be reached."},{"confidence":0.5,"severity":"Low","file":"src/lib/live-metric-coverage-reader.ts","area":"performance / availability","impact":"wp20_metric_registration_revision is a COUNT over an append-only ledger that keeps growing. It runs once per candidate row in the reader's WHERE clause (up to 10001 rows) and twice per audit page. Over time this can hit statement_timeout and leave coverage unavailable even when it is truthfully complete.","required_test":"Seed a ledger with more than 1M events and more than 1k proof rows, then check reader and audit latency stay within budget.","issue":"An expensive per-live COUNT is evaluated per row or per page instead of once.","evidence":"Reader lines 24-25 call the function with column arguments. Audit context line 50 runs on every forward and reverse page.","recommended_fix":"Compute the revision once into a CTE or parameter and compare against that, or keep a counter maintained in the same transaction as the ledger insert."},{"confidence":0.5,"severity":"Low","file":"src/lib/live-metric-registration-coverage.ts","area":"write race reporting","impact":"If a source change commits between the publisher's revision SELECT and its INSERT, the guard trigger raises error 23514 and the publisher throws, instead of returning source_changed. It fails closed, but the outcome is not reported truthfully, and retry logic may treat it as an unexpected failure.","required_test":"Inject a committed source change between the revision read and the INSERT, and check that the publisher returns {status:'source_changed'} and that no row is written.","issue":"The guard's revision-mismatch exception is not mapped to a status.","evidence":"Lines 23-30 have no error handling. Migration 2 lines 10-11 raise the exception.","recommended_fix":"Catch SQLSTATE 23514 with the registration or revision messages and map it to source_changed. Alternatively, take an advisory or row lock that serializes source-ledger appends for the live during the check and insert."},{"confidence":0.7,"severity":"Low","file":"scripts/wp20-registration-matched-audit.mjs","area":"test coverage","impact":"Several refusal paths have no runtime evidence, so a regression could go undetected: cross-tenant scope, form_mismatch, other_version, identity_mismatch, missing_registration, registration_without_capture, capture_mismatch, projection changes after publish, and limit_exceeded.","required_test":"Add negative cases: wrong vendorId or liveId returns unavailable; each mismatch outcome makes the publisher return 'incomplete'; changing a projection row after publish invalidates coverage; a small injected budget returns limit_exceeded; a concurrent write between the revision read and INSERT does not record a proof.","issue":"The fixture only covers the matched path, the empty path, a revoked source and a single race point.","evidence":"Lines 15-78 only assert matched, empty, the source flip before publish, and invalid_source after revoke.","recommended_fix":"Extend the fixture or add focused tests for the cases listed above, and clean up the FormSubmission rows explicitly in the finally block."}]}
